inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if it does not. Workers should not have to threaten a shutdown to make long-delayed negotiations a priority. The dispute highlights how institutions can depend on workers’ labor while leaving their concerns unresolved; the government needs to engage seriously and reach a fair agreement before university staff are pushed further into confrontation.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, or face an indefinite nationwide strike. That staff have had to threaten disruption just to get long-delayed talks treated as urgent shows how universities and government can rely on workers’ labor while sidelining their demands. The answer is not to blame workers for defending their rights, but for the government to negotiate seriously and reach a fair agreement before the dispute escalates further.
